item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 141126
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located several hundred
miles southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

&&
Public advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ25 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

...NORBERT HOLDING STEADY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.4N 137.8W
ABOUT 1125 MI...1810 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was
located near latitude 19.4 North, longitude 137.8 West. Norbert is
moving toward the west near 15 mph (24 km/h) and is expected to
maintain this general motion during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
A gradual weakening trend is forecast during the next couple of 
days, and Norbert could become a post-tropical cyclone tomorrow.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Bann/Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Sun Sep 13 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 140841
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Sun Sep 13 2026

A renewed burst of deep convection, with cloud-top temperatures as 
cold as -80 C, has developed over and east of Norbert's circulation 
center due to increasing westerly vertical wind shear. Despite the 
recent increase in convection, an ASCAT-C scatterometer pass showed 
an asymmetric wind field with peak winds of 34 kt north of the 
center. Based on these data, the initial intensity is lowered to 35 
kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be westward, or 280/11 kt. The 
storm remains positioned south of a subtropical ridge, which should 
steer Norbert on a general west-northwestward to westward track for 
the remainder of the forecast period. The track guidance remains in 
fairly good agreement, and the NHC track forecast is largely 
unchanged, reflecting a blend of the previous forecast with the 
latest HFIP corrected consensus approach (HCCA) and Google DeepMind 
ensemble mean (GDMI).

A combination of mid-level dry air and strengthening westerly 
vertical wind shear should make it increasingly difficult for 
Norbert to maintain organized deep convection, resulting in a steady 
weakening trend over the next couple of days. The current NHC 
intensity forecast is largely an update of the previous advisory and 
shows Norbert degenerating into a remnant low by Tuesday and 
dissipating as it opens into a trough by Wednesday.

--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression 
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 16.3 North, longitude 119.7 
West. The depression is moving toward the west-southwest near 9 mph 
(15 km/h) and this motion is expected to continue for the next 
several days with some gradual acceleration.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some slight strengthening is forecast during the next 24 hours, and
the depression could become a tropical storm later today. The
system is expected to weaken beginning Tuesday night or Wednesday.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026 
705 
WTPZ45 KNHC 141434
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
800 AM PDT Mon Sep 14 2026
 
The center of the tropical depression remains on the western edge of
the convection due to ongoing westerly shear. The most recent TAFB
Dvorak fix was T2.0/30 kt, while the UW-CIMSS objective intensity
estimates are in the range of 27-34 kt. Therefore, the initial
intensity is being held at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The tropical depression continues to move west-southwest
with an initial motion of 240/8 kt. This seems to be due to a
combination of the nearby convection and the overall system being
steered by a low- to mid-level ridge to the northwest. This ridge
should continue to be the main steering flow for the cyclone and
increase overall forward speed later in the forecast period. The
current NHC forecast track has been adjusted slightly right of the
previous track and just a bit slower than before. The current
forecast track is closer to the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach
(HCCA) and Google DeepMind (GDMI) forecast aids.
 
The environment is not expected to be very conducive for too much
strengthening due to the moderate northwesterly vertical wind shear
advecting some dry air into the center of the depression. Despite
this, the intensity guidance shows the possibility of some 
strengthening during the next 24 h. Based on this, the NHC 
intensity forecast calls for some slight strengthening. While there 
is a period between 24-48 h where the shear should weaken, the 
guidance suggests that the cyclone will not be able to take 
advantage of this period to strengthen. After 48 h, the cyclone 
should weaken as it gets lost within the larger monsoon trough. The 
NHC intensity forecast is similar to the prior advisory, but keeps 
35 kt intensity for a little while longer.
